name: security-opensearch-snapshot-authority-review
intent: OpenSearch snapshot repository registration and restore authority
artifacts: Snapshot roles, repository settings, external storage identity and restore/index selection permissions.
trace: Follow who may create/change repository destinations or restore data into indexes with different confidentiality/authorization semantics.
experiment: Use an isolated owned cluster and synthetic snapshot repository; compare permitted backup/restore and an out-of-policy repository/index selection.
disproof: Snapshot listing is not data extraction, and an administrator-authorized restore is not a tenant bypass.
repair: Constrain repository/restore authority and storage credentials, verifying legitimate recovery and tenant separation.
branch_decisions: Separate repository registration, snapshot creation, restore and security-index restrictions. Restoring an owned snapshot into an allowed test index may be intended. Inspect whether the caller can select another tenant data or privileged index, and whether repository credentials belong to the node service; do not execute production restores or list unknown backup contents.
operational_method: Collect security-plugin/version settings, permitted restore APIs, selected indices and whether global/security state can be included. Separate repository registration/storage credentials used by the node from the caller allowed to restore into an index. Inspect the actual registration and restore checks plus a supplied or isolated denied-index control; an object-store credential held by the node does not itself grant a tenant snapshot or cluster-state authority.
